questions.question: Jitin's age 3 years from now will be double the average of Jitin's current age and his age 8 years ago. What was Jitin's age 5 years ago?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Double the **average** of two values is always equal to their **sum**.

Age 3 years from now = (**Current age**) + (**Age 8 years ago**)

Current age + 3 = Current age + (Current age − 8)

3 = Current age − 8 ⇒ **Current age** = 11 years.

Jitin's age 5 years ago = 11 − 5 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let **Jitin's current age** be J.

Age 3 years from now = J + 3

Age 8 years ago = J − 8

**Formula Used:**

Average of two numbers A and B = (A + B) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe0bfdf3fd88f60927e7c16c198e2c7627db092978fd3dfcb3f5144a4ff7952c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average of current age and age 8 years ago = [J + (J − 8)] ÷ 2

⇒ Average = (2J − 8) ÷ 2 = J − 4

⇒ According to the question: (J + 3) = 2 × (J − 4)

⇒ J + 3 = 2J − 8

⇒ 2J − J = 8 + 3

⇒ J = 11 years

⇒ Jitin's age 5 years ago = J − 5 = 11 − 5 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Representation of Ages

If the current age is x, then age after n years is (x + n) and age n years ago was (x − n).

Average of Ages

The average of ages of n people is the sum of their individual ages divided by n.

Ratio and Proportions in Ages

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant throughout their lives, which is a key property for solving ratio-based age problems.</p

questions.question: Which organ in the human body helps to maintain balance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ear**__.

__
 
• The **Ears** perform two sensory functions, **hearing** and **maintenance of body balance**.__

 

The ear plays an essential role in maintaining the body's balance. This balance system of the body is often known as the **vestibular system,** and it's primarily located in the inner ear, specifically in the structures called the semicircular canals and the otolithic organs (the utricle and the saccule).

__
 
• **The Semicircular Canals**: These canals are filled with a fluid called endolymph and contain hair cells (sensory receptors). Each of the three semicircular canals corresponds to a different plane of motion: one for horizontal (left and right), one for vertical (up and down), and one for tilting movements. When the head moves, fluid inside the semicircular canals moves and stimulates the hair cells. The hair cells then send signals about the movements to the brain.
 
• **The Otolithic Organs (the Utricle and the Saccule):** These organs help to detect linear movements (forward, backward, sideways) and also the gravity. They contain tiny calcium carbonate crystals (otoconia) over a layer of hair cells. When the head moves, these crystals also move, causing the hair cells to bend and thus send signals to your brain about the head and body's motion and position.​

questions.question: The perimeter of a parallelogram is 48 cm. If the height of the parallelogram is 6 cm and the length of the adjacent side is 8 cm, find its area.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of adjacent sides = **Perimeter** ÷ 2 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 cm.

Base of the parallelogram = 24 − 8 = 16 cm.

**Area** = Base × Height = 16 × 6 = 96 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Perimeter** of parallelogram = 48 cm

⇒ Length of one **adjacent side** (b) = 8 cm

⇒ **Height** (h) of the parallelogram = 6 cm

**Formula used:**

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (Side₁ + Side₂)

⇒ Area = **Base** × **Height**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3afbec8c23573d2d29d13f48ddab286acb88782c07749c12adccadb17d97f34c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 48 = 2 × (Base + 8)

⇒ 24 = Base + 8

⇒ **Base** = 24 − 8 = 16 cm

⇒ **Area** = 16 × 6

⇒ **Area** = 96 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Parallelogram

The area can be calculated as Area = a × b × sin(θ), where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the angle between them.

Height and Side Relationship

In a parallelogram, the product of a side and its corresponding altitude is constant: Area = Base₁ × Height₁ = Base₂ × Height₂.

Properties of Parallelogram

Opposite sides are equal and parallel, and diagonals bisect each other.</p

questions.question: If x² + y² = 6 and x³y + xy³ + x² + y² = 36, then the value of xy is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Factor out the **common factor** (x² + y²) from the given expression: xy(x² + y²) + (x² + y²) = 36

Substitute the value x² + y² = 6 into the equation: 6(xy) + 6 = 36

⇒ 6(xy + 1) = 36

⇒ xy + 1 = 6 ⇒ xy = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x² + y² = 6 --- (1)

x³y + xy³ + x² + y² = 36 --- (2)

**Method: Factorization by grouping**

⇒ xy(x² + y²) + (x² + y²) = 36

⇒ (x² + y²)(xy + 1) = 36

**Substitute** the value of (x² + y²) from equation (1):

⇒ 6 × (xy + 1) = 36

⇒ xy + 1 = 36 ÷ 6

⇒ xy + 1 = 6

⇒ xy = 6 − 1

⇒ xy = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Factorization by Grouping

This method involves rearranging the terms of a **polynomial** into groups that share a **common factor**, such as a(x + y) + b(x + y) = (a + b)(x + y).

Algebraic Identity for Squares

The square of a **binomial** is given by (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy. This is useful for finding the sum of squares when the product is known.

Substitution Method

In a **system of equations**, a known value or expression from one equation is substituted into another to reduce the number of **variables** and solve the problem.</p

questions.question: Some items are purchased for Rs 4,500. If one-third of the articles are sold at a loss of 15%, then at what percentage profit should the remaining articles be sold, so that a profit of 20% is earned on the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total items are divided into **3 parts** (since 1/3 is sold first).

Let the total quantity be 3 units. 1 unit is sold at **15% loss** (−15).

Remaining 2 units must be sold at **x% profit** (+x).

Total target profit is **20%** on 3 units: 3 × 20 = 60.

Equation: 1 × (−15) + 2 × x = 60 ⇒ 2x = 60 + 15 = 75 ⇒ x = 37.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Total CP** = Rs 4,500, **Total Profit** = 20%, **Loss on 1/3** = 15%.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100 | Total Profit = (P1 + P2 + ...)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6681e485dfe2481594c88c3bac85de5713f441914f49ce76c248092345db8ee.png] 
⇒ Total **required SP** = 4500 × (120/100) = **Rs 5,400**.
⇒ CP of 1/3 articles = 4500 ÷ 3 = **Rs 1,500**.
⇒ SP of 1/3 articles = 1500 × (85/100) = **Rs 1,275**.
⇒ Remaining CP = 4500 − 1500 = **Rs 3,000**.
⇒ Required SP of remaining = 5400 − 1275 = **Rs 4,125**.
⇒ Profit needed = 4125 − 3000 = **Rs 1,125**.
⇒ Profit% = (1125 ÷ 3000) × 100 = **37.5%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Method

When parts of goods are sold at different profit/loss rates, the overall profit/loss is the weighted average: Total% = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) / (n₁ + n₂).

Independence from Absolute Value

In percentage-based profit/loss questions involving parts of a whole, the **actual Cost Price** (Rs 4,500) does not affect the final percentage result and can be ignored for faster calculation.</p

questions.question: What is the least value of x for which the number 712x816 is divisible by 12?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 12 ⇒ Number must be divisible by 3 and 4.

For 4: Last two digits 16 are divisible by 4 (True).

For 3: Sum of digits (7+1+2+x+8+1+6) = 25 + x must be divisible by 3.

Nearest multiples of 3 > 25 are 27, 30, 33.

For least value: 25 + x = 27 ⇒ x = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 712x816, Divisor = 12

**Formula Used:** Divisibility rule of 12 (divisible by 3 and 4).

 
 7 1 2 x 8 1 6
 

 Sum of digits (Rule of 3)
 
 Check: 16 ÷ 4

Check Divisibility by 4:

⇒ Last two digits of 712x816 = 16

⇒ 16 ÷ 4 = 4 (Remainder = 0)

⇒ The number is divisible by 4 for any value of x.

Check Divisibility by 3:

⇒ Sum of digits = 7 + 1 + 2 + x + 8 + 1 + 6

⇒ Sum = 25 + x

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 3, (25 + x) must be a multiple of 3.

⇒ Possible values for (25 + x) are 27, 30, 33, ...

⇒ For least value of x: 25 + x = 27

⇒ x = 27 − 25

⇒ x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the last two digits of the number are divisible by 4 or are 00.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Composite Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, it is also divisible by their product (a × b). Example: 12 = 3 × 4.</p

questions.question: The average of the first five natural numbers is 3. Find a new average after adding 6.
questions.solution:

Change in **average** = (New Value − Old Average) ÷ New Total Count

New **average** = 3 + 0.5 = 3.5

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

**Average** of the first 5 **natural numbers** = 3

New **observation** added = 6

**Average** = **Sum of observations** ÷ **Total count**

⇒ **New total count** of numbers = 5 + 1 = 6

⇒ **New average** = 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average of n natural numbers

The **average** of the first n **natural numbers** is calculated using the formula: (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of n natural numbers

The total **sum** of the first n **natural numbers** is given by the expression: [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in **Arithmetic Progression**, the **average** is always (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of the equation 2x² - 3x - 5 = 0, then the quadratic equation whose roots are (alpha)/(beta) and (beta)/(alpha) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0 having **roots** α and β, the equation with roots α/β and β/α is given by the formula: **acx² − (b² − 2ac)x + ac = 0**.

Given: a = 2, b = −3, c = −5.

Substitute values: (2 × −5)x² − [(−3)² − 2(2)(−5)]x + (2 × −5) = 0

⇒ −10x² − [9 + 20]x − 10 = 0 ⇒ −10x² − 29x − 10 = 0

Multiply the entire equation by −1: 10x² + 29x + 10 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 10x² + 29x + 10 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Equation 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0 with roots **α** and **β**.

**Formula Used:**

1. **Sum of roots** (α + β) = −b/a

2. **Product of roots** (αβ) = c/a

3. New **quadratic equation**: x² − (Sum of new roots)x + (Product of new roots) = 0

**Calculations:**

⇒ α + β = −(−3)/2 = 3/2

⇒ αβ = −5/2

Let the new roots be **y₁ = α/β** and **y₂ = β/α**.

⇒ Sum of new roots (S) = α/β + β/α = (α² + β²) / αβ

⇒ S = [(α + β)² − 2αβ] / αβ

⇒ S = [(3/2)² − 2(−5/2)] / (−5/2) = [9/4 + 5] / (−5/2)

⇒ S = (29/4) / (−5/2) = (29/4) × (−2/5) = −29/10

⇒ Product of new roots (P) = (α/β) × (β/α) = 1

⇒ Required Equation: x² − (−29/10)x + 1 = 0

⇒ x² + 29x/10 + 1 = 0 ⇒ 10x² + 29x + 10 = 0

This corresponds to **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10x² + 29x + 10 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The **discriminant** D = b² − 4ac determines the nature: D > 0 means real and distinct roots, D = 0 means real and equal, and D < 0 means imaginary roots.

Transformation of Equations

If roots are replaced by their **reciprocals** (1/α, 1/β), the new equation is obtained by swapping 'a' and 'c' (cx² + bx + a = 0).

Vieta's Formulas

For a **polynomial** of any degree, the sum of roots taken one at a time is always −(coefficient of next highest power) / (leading coefficient).</p

questions.question: When were privy purses officially abolished in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Privy purses were annual payments made to the rulers of erstwhile princely states as part of the integration of these states into the Indian Union post-independence.
 
• These payments were guaranteed under Articles 291 and 362 of the Indian Constitution to ensure the cooperation of princely states during the process of integration.
 
• In 1971, under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, the 26th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted, officially abolishing privy purses.
 
• The 26th Amendment removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution and abolished the recognition of rulers as well as their privileges.
 
• The move was part of the broader effort to promote equality and eliminate the remnants of feudalism in independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privy Purses:**

 
 
• Privy purses were monetary allowances given to the rulers of princely states as part of their agreement to join India.
 
• The amount varied based on the size, revenue, and status of the princely state.
 
 
 
• **26th Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• This amendment was passed in 1971 and removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Indian Constitution.
 
• It ended the recognition of princely states and abolished all privileges, titles, and privy purses associated with them.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition of privy purses was seen as a step toward reducing inequality and strengthening the democratic fabric of India.
 
• It also marked the end of any feudal privileges and ensured that all citizens were treated equally under the law.
 
 
 
• **Integration of Princely States:**
 
 
• Post-independence, there were more than 550 princely states in India.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon played key roles in integrating these states into the Indian Union through diplomacy and negotiation.

questions.question: Aman started a business investing 70000 rs. Rakhi joined him after six months with an amount of 105000 rs. and Sagar joined them with 1.4 lakhs rs. after another six months. questions.question: A 1.5 m tall boy is standing at a distance of 3 m from a 4 m high light post. The light from top of post casts his shadow. What is the length of the boy's shadow?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For problems involving shadows and **similar triangles**, use the direct formula:

**Shadow Length** = (**Boy height** × **Distance from post**) ÷ (**Post height** − **Boy height**)

⇒ Shadow = (1.5 × 3) ÷ (4 − 1.5)

⇒ Shadow = 4.5 ÷ 2.5 = 1.8 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the **light post** (H) = 4 m

Height of the **boy** (h) = 1.5 m

**Distance** of the boy from the post (d) = 3 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7914bdfb6902eb83205ace1a28aa6f412d0948611b61004b7216639083f4159e.png] 

By the property of **Similar Triangles**, the ratio of the height to the total base is constant:

⇒ (Height of Post) ÷ (Distance + Shadow) = (Height of Boy) ÷ Shadow

Let the length of the **shadow** be s.

⇒ 4 ÷ (3 + s) = 1.5 ÷ s

⇒ 4 × s = 1.5 × (3 + s)

⇒ 4s = 4.5 + 1.5s

⇒ 4s − 1.5s = 4.5

⇒ 2.5s = 4.5

⇒ s = 4.5 ÷ 2.5

⇒ s = 1.8 m

Comparing this result with the given options, we find that **Option (2)** matches the calculated value.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal; consequently, the ratios of their **corresponding sides** are equal (Side-Side-Side similarity).

Angle of Elevation

In shadow problems, the **angle of elevation** of the light source is the same for all objects at the same time, creating similar right-angled triangles.

Shadow Inversion Rule

For a fixed object height, as the object moves **closer** to the light source, the shadow length **increases**, and as it moves away, the shadow **decreases**.</p

questions.question: An alloy contains copper and tin in the ratio 3 ∶ 2. If 250gm of copper is added to this alloy then the copper in it becomes double the quantity of tin in it. What is the amount (in gm) of tin in the alloy?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **ratio** of **Copper** : **Tin** = 3 : 2. Final ratio = 2 : 1.

Since only **Copper** is added, keep **Tin** constant by multiplying the final ratio by 2.

New ratios → Initial 3 : 2 | Final 4 : 2. Difference in **Copper** = 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

Given 1 unit = 250 gm. Therefore, **Tin** = 2 units = 2 × 250 gm = 500 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 500 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial ratio **Copper** : **Tin** = 3 : 2. Added **Copper** = 250 gm. Final ratio = 2 : 1.

**Formula Used:** Ratio × constant = Actual quantity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/684f1edba99adc36c79240aeafce664c56b8331facd9348b198dd604c5566de7.png] 

Let the initial quantity of **Copper** be 3x and **Tin** be 2x.

⇒ New **Copper** = 3x + 250

⇒ (3x + 250) ÷ 2x = 2 ÷ 1

⇒ 3x + 250 = 4x

⇒ 4x − 3x = 250

⇒ x = 250

⇒ Amount of **Tin** = 2x = 2 × 250 = 500 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 500 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Quantity Concept

In a mixture, if only one component is added or removed, the quantity of the other component remains constant. We can solve such problems by equalizing the ratio units of the constant component.

Ratio Balancing

To balance two ratios a : b and c : d when 'b' must be equal to 'd', multiply the first ratio by 'd' and the second ratio by 'b'.

Alligation Method

This problem can also be solved by **Alligation** by treating pure copper as a 100% copper mixture and comparing it with the copper percentages in the alloy before and after the addition.</p

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from Stations A and B respectively and travel towards each other at a speed of 60 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. At the time they meet, the faster train has travelled 60 km more than the slower train. What is the distance between the two stations?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In the same time, the **ratio of distances** is equal to the **ratio of speeds**.

Ratio of speeds = 60 : 40 = **3 : 2**

Difference in distance ratio = 3 − 2 = **1 unit**

Given 1 unit = 60 km

Total distance ratio = 3 + 2 = 5 units ⇒ 5 × 60 = **300 km**

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Train 1** (v₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of **Train 2** (v₂) = 40 km/h

Difference in distance covered = 60 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8d59ce5ab449c840965009b31384b08be4e89731d0f8687dbf7d801ce20d2e6.png] 

**Formula:**

Time (t) = Difference in Distance ÷ Difference in Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference in speed = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet (t) = 60 ÷ 20 = **3 hours**

⇒ Distance traveled by Train 1 = 60 × 3 = 180 km

⇒ Distance traveled by Train 2 = 40 × 3 = 120 km

⇒ Total distance between A and B = 180 + 120 = **300 km**

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other (opposite direction), relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When they move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Meeting Time Formula

Time taken to meet = Initial distance between objects ÷ Relative speed. In this problem, Total Distance = (S₁ + S₂) × t.

Constant Time Property

If time is constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the speed (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).</p

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using a firewall on a Personal Computer?

options.text: To block unauthorised access and protect the computer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To block unauthorised access and protect the computer**__.

__
 
• A **firewall** is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's previously established security policies.
 
• Its primary purpose is to establish a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks, such as the internet.
 
• Firewalls can be hardware-based, software-based, or a combination of both.
 
• They can prevent unauthorized access to or from a private network and are essential for protecting sensitive data and resources.
 
• Firewalls use various techniques to control traffic, including packet filtering, proxy service, and stateful inspection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Firewalls can also be used to log and report on network activity, which can help in identifying suspicious activity and troubleshooting network issues.
 
• Modern firewalls can inspect secure sockets layer (SSL) and transport layer security (TLS) encrypted traffic to ensure that threats don't hide in encrypted connections.
 
• Advanced firewalls offer additional features, such as intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDPS), and can integrate with other security tools like antivirus software.
 
• The concept of a firewall originated from the physical firewalls used in buildings to prevent the spread of fire.

questions.question: What happens when a computer is put into Sleep mode?

• **Option 4 – It restarts automatically after a few minutes:** ❌ Incorrect. The system remains idle until the user wakes it up.

questions.question: The scope of the Article 21 of the Constitution was expanded to include Right of Education, because of the decision of Supreme Court in the case

options.text: Govind v/s State of Madhya Pradesh
Parmanand Katara v/s Union of India
Chameli Singh v/s State of Uttar Paradesh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unnikrishnan v/s Andhra Pradesh.**__

 
• The right to education became a fundamental right by the **86th amendment of 2002.**
 
• The scope of Article 21 of the constitution was expanded to include the Right of Education, because of the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of **Unnikrishnan **v/s** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
 
• The Supreme court’s landmark judgment in the Unnikrishnan JP vs State of Andhra Pradesh was in **1993.**
 
• This case expressed disagreement with the finding in the earlier case of **Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka 1992.**
 
 
 
• The 86th constitutional amendment inserted **Article 21 A** into the Indian constitution.
 
• Article 21 A says that the state shall provide free and compulsory education to all children in the **age-group of 6-14. **
 
• The Right to education act came into force on **1st April 2010.**
 
• The case of **Govind v. State of Madhya Pradesh **is the landmark case associated with the **right to privacy.**
 
• The case of **Parmanand Katara v/s Union of India** is associated with the obligation on the State to preserve life.
 
• The case of **Chameli Singh v/s State of Uttar Pradesh** is associated with the right to shelter as a component of the right to life under Article 21 and freedom of movement under Article 19(1)(e).

options.text: Both I and II are strong

questions.solution:
• The statement is talking about linking the rivers. The argument I claims that linking the rivers will lead to complete “eradication of water shortage in remote areas”. Hence, argument I is strong.
 
• Argument II is talking about “river contamination” which is not mentioned in the statement at all.
 
• Hence, only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Place the following ruler of Magadha in their chronological order of rule:

A. Bindusara

B. Bimbisara

C. Ashoka

D. Ajatasatru
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B, D, A, C.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Magadha Empire**

 
• The Magadha Empire ruled from 684 B.C - 320 B.C in India.
 
• The reference of the Magadha Empire is found in the two great epics Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• There were three dynasties who ruled the Magadha empire from 544 BC to 322 BC.
 
• The first one was the **Haryanka dynasty (544 BC to 412 BC)**, the second was **Shisunaga Dynasty (412 BC to 344 BC)** and the other one was the **Nanda dynasty (344 BC-322 BC).**
 
• **Bimbisara came from the Haryanka dynasty, ruled for 52 years from 544 B.C. to 492 B.C**.
 
• **Bimbisara was imprisoned by his son Ajatshatru who ruled Magadha empire from 492- 460 B.C. He murdered his father Bimbisara.**
 
• **Bindusara** was the son of **Chandragupta Maurya**, the **founder of Maurya dynasty** and ruled from **298 BC to 272 BC. **He is also referred to as Amitraghata (amitra-enemy, ghata-slayer) in Sanskrit Literature. Strabo has named him Amitrochates or Allitrochades which are a greek version of the name Amitraghata. He had two sons Sumana & Ashoka. Ashoka later succeeded him, after his death.
 
• **Ashoka** was the son of Bindusara. He was governor of Taxila and Ujjain during his father’s reign. **Ashoka sat on the throne around 268 B.C** after successfully defeating his brothers. Hence option 3 is correct.
